tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies on the tower above the walled town in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780). No other flag is shown, so the pictures never say who held the Rock before that or who the attackers are.

tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger directly. The most they suggest is that land and sea are cut off: a siege camp, a convoy line, and ships circling offshore. There is no food, starving people or text about hunger.
tra_loi.Q4: Ships. A fleet of sailing ships approaches the town in Jan 1780 (frame 47), and a column of small figures with red cargo or barrels reaches the bastion (frames 48-49). The pictures don't say if these are a relief fleet, and they don't clearly show that the town is rescued.

tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies on the tower above the walled town in frames 40–41 (14 Jan 1780), and red-coated soldiers stand on the slope below it. Nothing on screen names the nation, so this rests on the flag and uniforms.
tra_loi.Q2: The Great Siege. Frame 23 shows the caption '1779 — The Great Siege' and the date 21 Jun 1779. After that, the camp of rows of white tents grows beside the town (frames 27–33), and ships ring the bay.
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger or empty stores directly. The likely cause is that the town is cut off: a large tent camp is built on the land side (frames 27–33) and ships sit offshore (frames 34–39, 53–56). A lone line of animals walking toward the town is the only hint about food, and it is ambiguous.
tra_loi.Q4: A fleet of ships arrives by sea. On 18 Jan 1780 (frame 47) a group of sailing ships approaches the coast. In frames 48–49 people unload red-brown barrels or supplies on a quay under the walls, which looks like food or supplies being delivered. Whose fleet it is is not shown. Frames 52–56 show more ships on 12 Apr 1781, but the pictures do not make clear whether these are relief ships or enemy ships.
